newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude weaken, ADNOC premiums over Dubai rise.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weaken, ADNOC premiums over Dubai rise.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were weaker on Tuesday, undermined by a fall in futures prices, with interest subdued ahead of official monthly crude price announcements.
SIMEX Brent November futures fell 31 cents to $22.90 and the fall continued during London hours with the contract falling as low as $22.75. Support was seen at $22.65.
NYMEX November crude, trading on ACCESS, fell to $23.98 in late afternoon dealings, down from $24.38 in New York Monday.
The fall weighed on Tapis paper, which was notionally bid at $22.85 on November. Futures volatility kept players sidelined.
ADNOC released its September prices for term lifters, which stretched premiums over Dubai. Murban was calculated at a $1.88 premium, Lower Zakum at $1.93 and Umm Shaif at $1.58.
Oman is expected to release its September term price in coming days, which could coincide with players bidding for the Bangchak November tender for Far East and Middle East crudes.
The tender closes on Wednesday and offers should be valid until Thursday.
In the wet market, a major sold 450,000 barrels of October Tapis. The deal was confirmed, but reports it was done at plus 90 cents were said to be "guessing."

Elsewhere, 300,000 barrels of October Bontang Mix traded into China at ICP flat to minus two cents in recent days. A further 250,000 barrels traded into China at ICP less one or two cents, traders said.
Minas was offered by a Japanese trader at ICP plus 15 to 20 cents.
